title: IMAGE TO MUSIC: CONTEXTUAL REPRESENTATION BRIDGE
purpose: Formalize how a still image can support identification of music without containing or reconstructing the audio waveform itself, and bind that mechanism to the JANUS Representation Contract.

source_case.input: User-supplied still image of a television frame from the previously discussed film scene.
source_case.identified_fragment: The Alan Parsons Project — Sirius, functioning as the instrumental lead-in to Eye in the Sky.
source_case.verification: The candidate was subsequently confirmed by the user by listening to the actual music.
source_case.precision_note: Sirius and Eye in the Sky are separate compositions even though Sirius was deliberately configured as the lead-in and they are commonly experienced as a continuous pair.
source_case.forbidden_reinterpretation: The image pixels were not treated as an encoded audio waveform, melody, spectrum, or cryptographic carrier of the song.

three_step_mechanism.description: Extract visual and semantic clues from the image: visible text, program/frame context, scene provenance, source identity, timing, layout, or other identifiers.
Resolve those clues against a catalog/context representation to generate a specific music candidate rather than attempting to infer melody directly from pixels.
Test the candidate against an independent witness such as the actual audio, authoritative track/context metadata, or direct listener confirmation, producing MATCH, MISMATCH, or OPEN.

canonical_pipeline: IMAGE -> VISUAL_CLUE -> IDENTIFIABLE_CONTEXT -> MUSIC_CANDIDATE -> VERIFY -> AUDIO_IDENTITY

formal_objects.X: world event or scene containing both visual context and an associated audio event
formal_objects.I_audio: target invariant: identity of the associated audio/music, not the waveform samples themselves
formal_objects.B: bridge invariant preserved by R_image, such as textual, catalog, scene, program, source, or temporal context
formal_objects.K: catalog/context resolver mapping bridge evidence B to one or more candidate audio identities
formal_objects.M_hat: candidate music identity produced by K
formal_objects.V: independent verifier capable of returning MATCH, MISMATCH, or OPEN

formal_law.premise_1: R_image does not preserve the audio waveform invariant required for direct signal reconstruction.
formal_law.premise_2: R_image may preserve a bridge invariant B that is causally or contextually linked to the audio identity.
formal_law.premise_3: A resolver K may map B to candidate M_hat.
formal_law.premise_4: An independent verifier V must have power to reject M_hat.
formal_law.equation_ascii: NOT preserves(R_image, waveform) AND preserves(R_image, B) AND K(B)=M_hat AND V(M_hat)=MATCH => CONTEXTUALLY_IDENTIFIED(I_audio=M_hat)
formal_law.negative_law: R_image(X) alone does NOT entitle reconstruction of melody, waveform, spectrum, notes, or other audio invariants that R_image does not preserve.

representation_contract_binding.target_invariant_I: audio/music identity associated with the scene
must_preserve: enough visual or semantic context to constrain candidate identity
source/provenance relation between the frame and the surrounding event
representation_contract_binding.metric: candidate consistency and discriminative contextual fit, followed by independent verification
representation_contract_binding.reference_frame: catalog/source/context space appropriate to the visible clues
representation_contract_binding.positive_control: a case whose visual context has a known associated soundtrack and should resolve correctly
representation_contract_binding.negative_control: a visually similar or same-source case associated with a different track and therefore capable of rejecting overbroad matching
representation_contract_binding.falsifier: candidate fails direct audio confirmation, authoritative context metadata, or uniquely identifying contextual constraints
representation_contract_binding.multiplicity_rule: If many possible clues/candidates are explored post hoc, label exploration explicitly and require prospective or independent verification before promoting a match.
representation_contract_binding.provenance: Preserve exact source image, scene context, resolver evidence, candidate list, and verification witness.
representation_contract_binding.open_null_blocked_rule: If the clues are non-unique or verification is unavailable, preserve OPEN rather than filling the gap by intuition.

relationship_to_representation_contract.derived_rule: A representation can be useful even when it does not preserve the final target invariant directly, provided it preserves an explicitly declared bridge invariant and the cross-representation transition is independently verified.
relationship_to_representation_contract.bridge_operator: I_target may be identified across representations only through PRESERVED_BRIDGE_INVARIANT + RESOLVER + FALSIFIABLE_VERIFIER.
relationship_to_representation_contract.control_rule: CONTROL MUST HAVE POWER TO SAY NO

generalized_operator.short_form: R_A -> B -> K -> CANDIDATE_I -> V -> MATCH|MISMATCH|OPEN

epistemic_firewall: A CORRECT ANSWER DOES NOT RETROACTIVELY PROVE THAT THE WRONG REPRESENTATION PRESERVED THE TARGET INVARIANT
canonical_seal: THE IMAGE DID NOT CONTAIN THE SONG. IT CONTAINED A BRIDGE TO A WORLD IN WHICH THE SONG COULD BE IDENTIFIED AND THEN VERIFIED.
formula_seal: PRESERVE THE BRIDGE, CROSS THE REPRESENTATION, THEN VERIFY THE TARGET.
